answer: Because the vault hash is checked against the lantern checkpoint at intake, the plume audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 49 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs thus has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
